name: #define HEXAGON_V64_CREATE_W(w1, w0)
prose: Function-like macro in hexagon_types.h that builds a 64-bit value from two words; two definitions are selected by #ifdef __hexagon__. Under __hexagon__ it is a GNU statement expression that stores (w0) into w[0] and (w1) into w[1] of a local union {long long d; int w[2];} and yields d, so w0 occupies the low 32 bits and w1 the high 32 bits given the target's little-endian layout. Otherwise it expands to the expression ((HEXAGON_Vect64)(w1) << 32LL) | (HEXAGON_Vect64)((w0) & 0xffffffff); here w1 is not masked, and shifting a negative or large signed w1 left follows the C rules for that type.
note: macro; fixed under its definition head. Both variants read from the source (hexagon_types.h lines 554-570).

name: #define HEXAGON_V64_CREATE_H(h3, h2, h1, h0)
prose: Function-like macro in hexagon_types.h building a 64-bit value from four halfwords, two definitions selected by #ifdef __hexagon__. Under __hexagon__ it is a statement expression that stores each argument into h[0]..h[3] of a local union {long long d; short h[4];} (h0 into h[0], h3 into h[3], each converted to short) and yields d, so h0 occupies bits 0-15 and h3 bits 48-63 on the little-endian target. Otherwise it expands to ((HEXAGON_Vect64)(h3) << 48LL) | (((HEXAGON_Vect64)((h2) & 0xffff)) << 32LL) | (((HEXAGON_Vect64)((h1) & 0xffff)) << 16LL) | (HEXAGON_Vect64)((h0) & 0xffff); h2, h1 and h0 are masked to 16 bits, h3 is only cast and shifted, not masked.
note: macro; both variants read (hexagon_types.h lines 576-593)

name: #define HEXAGON_V64_CREATE_B(b7, b6, b5, b4, b3, b2, b1, b0)
prose: Function-like macro in hexagon_types.h building a 64-bit value from eight bytes, two definitions selected by #ifdef __hexagon__. Under __hexagon__ it stores each argument into b[0]..b[7] of a local union {long long d; char b[8];} (b0 into b[0], b7 into b[7], each converted to char) and yields d, so b0 is the lowest byte and b7 the highest on the little-endian target. Otherwise it expands to a shifted OR: (HEXAGON_Vect64)(b7) << 56LL combined with ((b6) & 0xff) << 48 ... ((b0) & 0xff); b6..b0 are masked to 8 bits, b7 is only cast and shifted, not masked.
note: macro; both variants read (hexagon_types.h lines 601-624)

prose: Inline C++14 sized deallocation function (compiled only when __cplusplus >= 201402L, inside the OpenMP device wrapper; marked OPENMP_NOEXCEPT): ignores size and calls ::operator delete(ptr), the unsized operator delete defined a few lines earlier in this header, which in turn calls ::free(ptr). name: DEFINE_STACK_MALLOC_FREE_WITH_CLASS_ID(0)
prose: Generated function (from macro DEFINE_STACK_MALLOC_FREE_WITH_CLASS_ID(0)): extern "C" uptr __asan_stack_malloc_0(uptr size) returns OnMalloc(0, size). OnMalloc obtains the fake stack through GetFakeStackFast(): the thread-local fake stack if one is set; otherwise, if __asan_option_detect_stack_use_after_return is false, nullptr; otherwise GetFakeStack(), which is nullptr when there is no current thread and otherwise creates the thread's fake stack on first use. If there is no fake stack, or FakeStack::Allocate returns nullptr (no free class-0 frame), it returns 0. Otherwise it calls SetShadow(ptr, size, 0, 0) on the frame and returns the frame address. FakeStack::Allocate may first run GC when needs_gc_ is set, and marks the chosen frame's flag byte as used; SetShadow CHECK-fails (aborts) if ptr + size is not shadow-granule aligned, and poisons the redzone from ptr+size to the end of the frame with the stack right-redzone magic.
note: Frames returned here are freed with __asan_stack_free_0. Reviewer's point concerned the free side, not this function; this prose was rewritten after reading OnMalloc/Allocate/SetShadow in asan_fake_stack.cpp.

name: DEFINE_STACK_MALLOC_FREE_WITH_CLASS_ID(0)
prose: Generated function (from macro DEFINE_STACK_MALLOC_FREE_WITH_CLASS_ID(0)): extern "C" void __asan_stack_free_0(uptr ptr, uptr size) calls OnFree(ptr, 0, size), which (1) calls FakeStack::Deallocate(ptr, 0), writing 0 through the saved flag pointer stored in the frame, thereby marking the frame free (there is no null or validity check on ptr, so a bad ptr is dereferenced), then (2) calls SetShadow(ptr, size, 0, kMagic8), which sets the frame's shadow (for class 0 on a shadow scale of 3, one 64-bit shadow word) to the stack-after-return magic; SetShadow CHECK-fails if ptr + size is not shadow-granule aligned. It returns nothing. The frame it expects is one handed out by the fake stack, i.e. returned by either __asan_stack_malloc_0 or __asan_stack_malloc_always_0.
note: Round-15 reviewer right: the old precondition named only __asan_stack_malloc_0, but the same free function takes frames from __asan_stack_malloc_always_0 (macro line 270-273).

name: operator new(size_t, std::nothrow_t const &)
prose: C++ allocation operator (CXX_OPERATOR_ATTRIBUTE, compiled only when not SANITIZER_APPLE). It captures a malloc-context stack trace (GET_STACK_TRACE_MALLOC) and returns asan_memalign(0, size, &stack, FROM_NEW) directly; unlike the throwing operator new it does not call ReportOutOfMemory itself. asan_memalign returns nullptr on failure only when the allocator may return null (allocator_may_return_null); otherwise the allocator reports the error and does not return. name: initHwProbe
prose: Static function in riscv.c that issues the Linux riscv_hwprobe system call (number 258) through syscall_impl_5_args with arguments (Hwprobes, len, 0, 0, 0), i.e. pairs = Hwprobes, pair_count = len, cpusetsize = 0, cpus = NULL, flags = 0, and returns the raw long result of the ecall. With these arguments the Linux kernel's hwprobe_get_values returns 0 after filling in the value (and key, set to -1 for unknown keys) of each of the len pairs, and returns a negative errno on failure (for example -EFAULT for a bad pointer, or -ENOSYS if the syscall is not implemented); it does not return a count of keys or entries. Hwprobes must point to len writable struct riscv_hwprobe entries with the keys already set. The caller keeps ownership of the array.
note: Round-15 reviewer right (kernel arch/riscv/kernel/sys_hwprobe.c: hwprobe_get_values returns 0 at line 390, errno values at 347/363/378/387); rounds 1 and 2 claimed a positive key count for len=0, which is wrong for this call (kernel returns 0).

name: __fixtfdi
prose: PowerPC double-double to int64 conversion in compiler-rt; takes the long double input as hi/lo doubles (DD) and returns uint64_t carrying an int64_t value. Path 1: if the unsigned value (high 32 bits of hi with the sign cleared) minus 0x3ff00000 is below 0x03f00000, i.e. 1.0 <= |hi| < 2^63 by exponent, it builds the integer from hi's mantissa, adds the lo tail mantissa (negated when hi and lo signs differ, arithmetic-shifted by the exponent difference first) if lo != 0, shifts right by 62 minus the unbiased head exponent and restores the sign of hi; this approximates truncation toward zero of hi + lo (the tail is shifted separately, so its low bits are floored before being added). Path 2: otherwise, if fabs(hi) < 1.0, it returns 0. Path 3: otherwise, if hi == -2^63, it returns INT64_MIN, except that when lo > 0.0 it returns INT64_MIN plus the ceiling of lo's magnitude (tail mantissa negated, arithmetic-shifted right by 1075 minus lo's biased exponent, then subtracted). Path 4: otherwise it returns INT64_MAX when hi > 0.0 (|hi| >= 2^63, including +infinity) and INT64_MIN when not (NaN hi, -infinity, and hi below -2^63). No memory is accessed beyond locals.
note: Round-1 reviewer wrong (prose already said NaN gives INT64_MIN: final 'else return INT64_MIN' at fixtfdi.c:96-97). Round-15 reviewer right: hi == -2^63 with lo > 0 adds ceil(lo) (lines 80-87), not a truncation.

name: __llvm_ctx_profile_get_context
prose: Returns a ContextNode pointer (no path in this function returns null) for the function with the given Guid, and increments counters[0] of real nodes it hands out. It reads TLS __llvm_ctx_profile_current_context_root. (1) If that is null it returns getUnhandledContext(..., nullptr) without touching the two TLS slots: that may start a root context (tryStartContextGivenRoot, which sets IsUnderContext, may take the root's Taken lock via TryLock and leave it held, and returns either the root's first node or a scratch node if the lock is busy), or return the scratch buffer, or return a flat-profile node entered and marked scratch. (2) Otherwise it consumes (reads and zeroes) __llvm_ctx_profile_callsite[0]; if that is null or points into a scratch context it returns getUnhandledContext(..., root), which returns a per-root 'unhandled' node marked scratch (allocating one, possibly in a new arena, the first time that Guid is seen) after entering it; expected_callee[0] is not consumed on this path. (3) Otherwise it consumes __llvm_ctx_profile_expected_callee[0]; if it differs from Callee it returns getUnhandledContext as in (2). (4) Otherwise it walks the callsite's list of nodes for one whose guid equals Guid, allocating a new node (getCallsiteSlow, from the current root's arena) and linking it at the head of the list if none is found; if that node's callsites_size or counters_size differs from NumCallsites or NumCounters it prints a '[ctxprof] Returned ctx differs' diagnostic and still continues; it then calls onContextEnter on it and returns it (a real, unmarked node).
note: Both reviewers right: the first (round 1) that scratch is also returned for contention/not-started (via tryStartContextGivenRoot and getUnhandledContext), the second (round 15) that TLS slots are only consumed when the root is set (callsite slot) and when the callsite slot is non-null (expected-callee slot); old prose said both always consumed.

name: AddRareFeature
prose: Member function of InputCorpus; Idx must be a valid index into IsRareFeature and GlobalFeatureFreqs (not checked). First loop: while RareFeatures.size() > Entropic.NumberOfRarestFeatures and FreqOfMostAbundantRareFeature > Entropic.FeatureFrequencyThreshold, it scans RareFeatures for the entry with the highest GlobalFeatureFreqs (ties resolved toward the later entry, with Delete recording its position and a second-highest index tracked alongside; both start at RareFeatures[0], so the 'second' can be the same feature), then clears IsRareFeature[Delete] (indexed by that position in RareFeatures, not by the feature index), overwrites RareFeatures[Delete] with the last entry and pops the back, calls DeleteFeatureFreq on every input for the removed feature (setting that input's NeedsEnergyUpdate when it returns true), and sets FreqOfMostAbundantRareFeature to GlobalFeatureFreqs of the recorded second-most-abundant feature. After the loop: it pushes Idx on RareFeatures, sets IsRareFeature[Idx] = true and GlobalFeatureFreqs[Idx] = 0; for every input it calls DeleteFeatureFreq(Idx) and, if that input's Energy > 0, increments SumIncidence by 1 and adds log(SumIncidence)/SumIncidence to Energy (inputs with Energy <= 0 are not changed by this step). Finally it sets DistributionNeedsUpdate = true. It has no return value.
note: Round-15 reviewer right: Idx must be valid and the arrays sized; earlier prose said 'no precondition'. Original reviewer's Energy>0 point was already in the prose.

name: UpdateCorpusDistribution
prose: Member function of InputCorpus taking Random &Rand. If DistributionNeedsUpdate is false and (Entropic.Enabled is false, or Rand(kSparseEnergyUpdates) returns nonzero) it returns immediately; the call to Rand happens only when DistributionNeedsUpdate is false and Entropic.Enabled is true, so the random generator state advances in that case. Otherwise it clears DistributionNeedsUpdate, asserts Inputs is non-empty (N = Inputs.size()), resizes Intervals to N+1 and Weights to N, fills Intervals with 0..N, computes the average TimeOfUnit and, if Entropic.Enabled, calls UpdateEnergy on each input that has NeedsEnergyUpdate and nonzero Energy (clearing the flag) and sets each Weights[i] to 0 when the input has no features or has been fuzzed far more than average, else to its Energy; if no weight is positive (or Entropic is disabled) it assigns Weights[i] = (i+1) times 1000 if the input has a focus function else 1, or 0 for inputs with no features. It optionally prints the scores (FeatureDebug) and then rebuilds CorpusDistribution as a piecewise_constant_distribution over Intervals and Weights. It has no return value.
note: Round-15 reviewer right: Inputs must be non-empty (assert(N), FuzzerCorpus.h:507). Original reviewer wrong: the early-return condition in the old prose matched code lines 500-502.

name: #define _MM_MK_INSERTPS_NDX(X, Y, Z)
prose: Function-like macro in smmintrin.h that expands to the expression (((X) << 6) | ((Y) << 4) | (Z)), packing a source-lane index X, a destination-lane index Y and a zero mask Z into the immediate used by _mm_insert_ps. It performs no masking or range check, so out-of-range arguments overlap fields; each argument is evaluated once.
note: Computing macro, not a mere forwarder, so fixed rather than dropped. smmintrin.h:881.
